channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Ministros do STF dizem que Lula conta com reeleição ao insistir em Messias
item.description: Two Supreme Court ministers state that President Lula's insistence on appointing Jorge Messias to fill Luís Roberto Barroso's vacancy reflects his confidence in winning re-election in 2026. The move is interpreted as a signal that the government believes in its continued hold on power, despite political and judicial pressure surrounding the nomination. The action suggests strategic maneuvering to secure allies on the court ahead of potential electoral disputes.

item.title: Governo Lula estuda lançar o 'Desenrola' para adimplentes quitarem dívidas
item.description: The Lula government is considering launching a program called 'Desenrola' targeting debtors who are current on their payments but face financial strain to do so. The initiative aims to appeal to centrist voters by providing relief to those who maintain payment discipline despite economic hardship.

item.title: A postura de Lula às vésperas de análise da PEC do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: President Lula and his team are closely monitoring the vote on the PEC to end the 6×1 work schedule, following the withdrawal of a controversial Centrão amendment that would have allowed up to 52-hour weekly workweeks and a ten-year transition. The executive branch’s vigilance stems from fears of last-minute changes to the bill, which is a legislative priority for the government. Chamber President Hugo Motta aims to approve the PEC in both committee and plenary session on the same day, possibly next Thursday, after consulting with Lula to align the text with rapporteur Leo Prates.

item.title: A pesquisa Datafolha deu boas notícias para Lula, mas um dado dela ainda preocupa muito o PT
item.description: The Datafolha poll showed Lula's lead over Flávio Bolsonaro increased from three to nine percentage points in one week, indicating improved voter perception. However, a concerning detail for the PT is that Lula's rejection remains high among conservative sectors, which could hinder his growth in a potential runoff. Full access to the analysis is available only to subscribers.

item.title: Cinebiografia de Bolsonaro virou 'comédia de erros' que ameaça candidatura de Flávio, diz 'Financial Times'
item.description: The Financial Times reports that 'Dark Horse', a film financed by Flávio Bolsonaro with funds linked to banker Daniel Vorcaro — suspected of corruption and tied to the collapse of a US$10 billion bank — is turning into a 'comedy of errors' that threatens his 2026 pre-candidacy. Despite denying wrongdoing, the involvement raises doubts about his electoral viability, especially as Jair Bolsonaro, convicted of plotting a coup, remains the leader of Brazil’s right and the final arbiter of his son’s candidacy. The film has also drawn interest from allies like Steve Bannon, who sees potential for promotion in the U.S. among MAGA audiences.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro desembarca nos EUA à espera de encontro com Trump
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) arrived in the U.S. on Monday morning (May 25) expecting a meeting with President Donald Trump on Tuesday (May 26). Although allies claim the invitation came from the White House, there is no official confirmation, and concerns exist that Trump’s Iran negotiations may delay or cancel the meeting. Flávio aims to use the encounter to counter recent image damage from revelations about his contacts with banker Daniel Vorcaro and to showcase international prestige.

item.title: O futuro da direita não bolsonarista passa pela derrota de Flávio
item.description: The future of non-bolsonarist right-wing politics hinges on Flávio Bolsonaro's defeat, as he is portrayed as a weak and controversial copy of his father, tied to financial scandals and lacking charisma. His electoral prospects depend on external forces such as the Federal Police, Attorney General's Office, Electoral Court, and Supreme Court, alongside improving approval ratings for Lula's government, which have narrowed Flávio's deficit in polls.

item.title: A inegável prerrogativa constitucional do presidente de (re)indicação ao STF
item.description: The President of Brazil holds exclusive authority to nominate STF justices, subject to Senate approval. Even after senatorial rejection in the same legislative session, the Constitution does not bar re-nominating the same candidate, as nomination is an exclusive Executive function. Senate Mesa Directive No. 1/2010 cannot constitutionally restrict this power nor allow the Senate President to block the nomination prior to floor consideration.

item.title: Fim da 6x1: Governo quer votação unânime na Câmara nos moldes de isenção do IR
item.description: The Lula government seeks unanimous approval in the Chamber for ending the 6x1 work schedule, following the model of the income tax exemption for those earning up to R$ 5,000, which received cross-party support in October 2025. PEC rapporteur Deputy Leo Prates (Republicanos-BA) proposes exempting workers earning above R$ 16,900 monthly from the new work schedule and requested additional time to review the report, delaying the vote to Thursday, the 28th. The measure aims to reduce working hours with broad consensus, similar to the income tax reform.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro aposta em ‘Tropa de Elite’ digital para enfrentar crise do Master
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) has formed a 'Digital Elite Troop' of ten PL deputies with strong social media influence to defend his image and boost his 2026 pre-candidacy, in response to the scandal involving his ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro of the defunct Banco Master. The group operates in real time on social media, monitoring and countering left-wing attacks via a permanent WhatsApp coordination group, emphasizing organic follower mobilization and denying automation use.

item.title: Governo Lula corre contra o tempo para aprovar projetos de segurança antes das eleições
item.description: The Lula government is racing to approve 13 priority projects in justice and public security before the 2026 elections, including the Public Security PEC and measures against abusive fuel price hikes and environmental crimes. Despite the effort, the electoral period complicates legislative progress, and public security remains the government’s worst-rated area according to a Datafolha poll.

item.title: Cinebiografia de Bolsonaro virou 'comédia de erros' que ameaça candidatura de Flávio, diz Financial Times
item.description: The biopic Dark Horse, about Jair Bolsonaro and funded by Flávio Bolsonaro with money from banker Daniel Vorcaro — suspected of corruption — is triggering a political crisis threatening Flávio’s 2026 Senate bid, according to the Financial Times. The outlet says the funding raises doubts about his electoral viability, as Jair Bolsonaro, convicted of plotting a coup, remains the leader of Brazil’s right, with Flávio’s candidacy ultimately dependent on him.

item.title: ‘Dark Horse’: O que falta para lançar filme que abalou a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The biopic 'Dark Horse,' focusing on Flávio Bolsonaro's trajectory, is currently in post-production in the United States but faces potential blockage from Brazil's Ancine and TSE following a petition by Lula allies seeking to prevent its release before the 2026 elections. Described as potentially disruptive to Bolsonaro's campaign, the film remains inaccessible to the general public, available only to subscribers.

item.title: A decisão de Alexandre de Moraes que atrapalha a gestão da crise de Flávio Bolsonaro-Vorcaro
item.description: A decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, in effect for nearly four months, is hindering the management of the crisis involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro concerning audio exchanges about a R$ 61 million transfer for the film 'Dark Horse'. The injunction restricts access to evidence and communications, complicating defense efforts and transparency.

item.title: Somente Lula, Flávio e Renan Santos possuem militância própria
item.description: Only three presidential pre-candidates in 2026 — Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Renan Santos — have independent digital militias, according to monitoring of over 100,000 public WhatsApp groups between May 6 and 24. Romeu Zema and Ronaldo Caiado rely on borrowed mobilizations or traditional models without autonomous digital bases. In a country where political opinion is increasingly shaped online, having organic militancy is a first-order strategic advantage.

item.title: Motta se queixa de postura de Boulos ao Planalto, e líderes falam em prejuízo em negociações para fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta complained to President Lula and Planalto officials about Minister Guilherme Boulos’s conduct, claiming he intensifies debates and harms congressional negotiations, particularly on the PEC to end the 6x1 work scale and regulate app-based work. Motta urged Lula to speak with Boulos, but the president remained silent. Congressional leaders acknowledge Boulos’s political role but warn his approach stirs public opinion and complicates dialogue with lawmakers.

item.title: Indecisos veem desgaste de Flávio com ‘Dark horse’ e viés eleitoral em ações de Lula na área econômica
item.description: Undecided voters reject Flávio Bolsonaro’s explanations regarding the R$ 61 million request from Daniel Vorcaro for the 'Dark horse' film, finding them unconvincing and damaging to his image. Simultaneously, they express dissatisfaction with Lula’s economic measures, such as Desenrola 2.0, perceived as electoral tactics. The group rejects Bolsonaro-linked figures but also resents government efforts to boost popularity through isolated actions.

item.title: Arena digital: PT e PL antecipam guerra no TSE para conter uso de IA e associações a crises do Master e INSS
item.description: The PT and PL are already responsible for over 80% of the 79 electoral representations filed with the TSE as of last week, signaling an early legal battle four months ahead of the 2026 elections. While the PT pushes for stronger court action against AI-generated content, the PL seeks to curb the spread of videos linking Flávio Bolsonaro to scandals such as the Master Bank case.

item.title: Sob Lula, "estatal do Centrão" supera Bolsonaro com R$ 2,8 bilhões em doações
item.description: The Codevasf, a state-owned company linked to the Centrão bloc, allocated R$ 2.8 billion in donations of goods such as tractors, trucks, and sewing machines during Lula’s government (since January 2023), surpassing the R$ 2.6 billion (inflation-adjusted) distributed under Bolsonaro (2019-2022). Many of these donations were made via parliamentary amendments, lacking clear technical criteria and appearing to serve electoral purposes, according to CGU audits. The company claims its actions are technically sound and transparent, with meeting minutes and donation records published on its official website.

item.title: Veja escândalos que mudaram rumo de campanhas eleitorais no Brasil
item.description: Scandals involving Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro, linked to the extinguished Banco Master, emerged as the biggest electoral shock five months before the 2026 elections, raising suspicions of payments for a film and undue influence. While experts say such events rarely change the vote of ideologically convicted voters, they can erode trust in the political system and undermine candidacy viability, especially among moderate and undecided voters. Historical cases like Roseana Sarney’s in 2002 show scandals close to the election have greater potential to alter electoral outcomes.

item.title: RENAN SANTOS JÁ É O FENÔMENO DAS ELEIÇÕES 2026 - BOLSONARISTAS EM PÂNICO
item.description: Renan Santos is emerging as a central figure in speculation surrounding Brazil’s 2026 elections, gaining growing support among Bolsonaro allies who see him as a strong alternative to the current political landscape. His name has been increasingly linked to opposition movements against President Lula’s government, causing concern among presidential allies and energizing Bolsonarist bases that view him as a potential electoral phenomenon. Although he has not officially confirmed a candidacy, his rising visibility on social media and at conservative events already positions him as a name to watch.

item.title: A direita e o bolsonarismo diante do abalo na candidatura de Flávio - O Assunto #1726
item.description: The Datafolha poll following the 'Dark Horse' revelations about Flávio Bolsonaro's talks with Daniel Vorcaro showed electoral damage, with Lula at 40% and Flávio at 31% in the first round, and 46% rejecting him. Despite allies viewing his candidacy as 'toxic,' the right lacks a strong alternative, with other candidates stagnant or ambiguous. The 'Stockholm syndrome' of the right toward Bolsonarism explains its inability to distance itself from Flávio despite scandals.

item.title: Brasil precisa de uma Primeira Emenda igual à dos EUA
item.description: The content criticizes the Lula government for using Treasury funds to distribute populist benefits, such as abolishing the 'blusinhas tax', and for allegedly restricting freedom of expression through social media regulation. It argues these actions resemble a Santa Claus fantasy, with costs borne by the public treasury or fundamental rights. It suggests Brazil needs a First Amendment similar to the U.S. to protect free speech.

item.title: Maga se afasta de Trump e defende pautas ainda mais antidemocráticas para 2028
item.description: The MAGA (Make America Great Again) movement is distancing itself from Donald Trump and advocating even more antidemocratic policies for the 2028 elections, including ending women's voting rights and suppressing Black representation in the legislature. This ideological shift comes as parties prepare for the post-Trump era, with the right facing backlash from an unpopular government and the opposition seeking a unifying message to defeat Trumpism.

item.title: Messias deve se reunir com Lula para definir futuro após ser rejeitado pelo Senado para o STF
item.description: Advocacia General of the Union Minister Jorge Messias is expected to meet with President Lula after returning from vacation to discuss his future, particularly the possibility of a new nomination to the Supreme Court despite his April rejection by the Senate. The government argues there are legal loopholes to challenge the Senate's decision, claiming the restriction comes from an internal Senate act, not the Constitution, and that the issue is political, not procedural. Lula views the rejection as an affront to his constitutional authority to appoint ministers and intends to resend the nomination, with Messias or another candidate depending on reconciliation with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre.

item.title: Lula viaja ao Amazonas para tentar aparar arestas com aliados e fechar palanque
item.description: President Lula is traveling to Amazonas this Tuesday and Wednesday to build political alliances and finalize the electoral slate for the PT in the state, seeking to overcome MDB resistance to Marcelo Ramos as the Senate candidate. The Lula-backed gubernatorial candidate is Omar Azis (PSD), and Lula will also attend government events, including the delivery of Minha Casa, Minha Vida housing, visits to shipyards to announce Petrobras investments, and the launch of a BNDES-financed barge.

item.title: Lula define hoje decreto para subsidiar gasolina em R$ 0,44 por litro
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will review today a decree establishing a R$0.44 per liter gasoline subsidy to offset the impact of rising international oil prices, with an estimated monthly cost of R$1.2 billion, to be compensated by increased oil sector revenue. The measure, confirmed by Planning Minister Bruno Moretti, will be paid directly to producers and importers via ANP, while the government awaits congressional approval of a bill authorizing the use of extra oil revenues to subsidize fuels.

item.title: Lula e Motta se reúnem hoje para fechar texto da PEC do fim da escala 6x1: veja o que está em jogo
item.description: President Lula and House Speaker Hugo Motta are set to meet today to finalize the text of a constitutional amendment ending the 6x1 workweek, guaranteeing two days off per week and reducing the maximum workweek from 44 to 40 hours while maintaining current salaries. The proposal is considered a strategic priority for the Planalto and could bolster Lula’s 2026 re-election campaign, with pressure to approve it before the October elections. A vote in the special committee is expected later this week.

item.title: Desenrola 2.0: começa hoje uso do FGTS para renegociar dívidas. Veja as regras
item.description: Starting today, workers can use up to 20% of their FGTS balance or R$1,000 (whichever is higher) to renegotiate debts under Desenrola 2.0, prioritizing inactive accounts and releasing blocked anniversary withdrawal balances. The government estimates up to R$8.2 billion in FGTS funds will be used, plus an additional R$8.4 billion from 'forgotten money' in banks to cover potential defaults. This measure is part of Lula’s strategy to reduce household debt and gain electoral support ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Rumble e Trump Media notificam Moraes judicialmente por email
item.description: Lawyer Martin de Luca notified Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes by email regarding a lawsuit filed by Rumble and Trump Media & Technology Group in Florida. The companies claim Moraes’ orders removing Bolsonaro supporters’ profiles violate the U.S. First Amendment. Moraes has 21 days to respond; failure to do so may result in a default judgment.

item.title: Deputados cobram respeito de Lula após associação da Alerj à milícia
item.description: The Alerj demanded respect from President Lula after he stated that if the Assembly had to choose a governor for Rio de Janeiro, the pick would be a militiaman. The Assembly's statement called the remark unacceptable, emphasizing its democratic and legitimate nature, and urged institutional unity amid public security challenges. The comment was made during the inauguration of Fiocruz's CDTS, where Lula also urged acting governor Ricardo Couto to imprison 'all the thieves who governed' Rio, linking them to an organized militia.

item.title: Câmara acelera votação do fim da escala 6x1
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies is accelerating the vote on a Constitutional Amendment Proposal (PEC) aiming to abolish the 6x1 work schedule, with the final report's presentation and vote expected this week. If approved, the measure would change Brazil's working hour regulations, sparking debate among lawmakers, unions, and business sectors.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro: “Eu não tenho grupos”
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro denied the existence of a political group aligned with her that opposes Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential pre-candidacy. Her statement followed a Folha de S.Paulo report highlighting growing tensions between the senator’s allies and individuals close to Michelle. She emphasized she does not lead internal factions within the Bolsonarist movement.

item.title: Vinculado a Vorcaro, Flávio não aparece na Marcha para Jesus
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro avoided attending the March for Jesus in Rio de Janeiro, one week after proclaiming himself a representative of 'a project of God' in Sorocaba. His office stated he would remain in Brasília to speak with his father, Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest, without mentioning the reason for his absence from the religious event.

item.title: Lula chama Lava Jato de “grande mentira do século”; Moro rebate
item.description: President Lula labeled Operation Car Wash "the great lie of the 21st century" and accused the media of boosting the actions of former judge Sergio Moro and former prosecutor Deltan Dallagnol. The statement was made in an interview with the TV Brasil program Sem Censura on Friday, the 22nd.

item.title: Alerj rebate Lula após fala sobre ‘indicação de miliciano’
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro State Legislature (Alerj) pushed back against President Lula after he linked a potential legislative indication for the state government to militias, calling the statement 'unacceptable'. Alerj President Deputy Douglas Ruas (PL) said Lula disrespected the state and that neither he nor Mayor Eduardo Paes have the moral authority to lecture on fighting organized crime.

item.title: Joaquim Barbosa não autorizou vídeo de IA que o mostra como pré-candidato
item.description: Former STF minister Joaquim Barbosa denied authorizing or having knowledge of an AI-generated video portraying him as a pre-candidate for the Brazilian presidency. The video, published by a profile linked to the Christian Democracy party (DC), was released on Friday, the 22nd, and uses synthetic images to depict him in judicial robes. Barbosa stated he has no intention of running in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Ainda sem palanque em MG, Flávio Bolsonaro marca viagem ao estado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) will travel to Belo Horizonte on June 2 to meet with party leaders and attempt to define the Bolsonarist ticket in Minas Gerais, where there is still no consensus on launching an independent candidacy or supporting Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos). The PL is also considering Flávio Roscoe, former president of Fiemg, while Lula has not yet defined his support in the state, considered strategic as it is the country's second-largest electoral college.

item.title: Lula “foi pai que não tive”, disse Deolane em 2021
item.description: The opposition resurfaced a 2021 video in which lawyer Deolane Bezerra expressed admiration for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, calling him the 'father I never had'. The video emerged after her arrest in May 2026 on suspicion of involvement in a money laundering scheme linked to the PCC. Flávio and Carlos Bolsonaro shared images of Bezerra with Lula, sparking political discussion.

item.title: Flávio, sobre uso de colete: “Não posso dar sopa para o azar”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-SP), a pre-candidate for the 2026 Brazilian presidency, announced he is now wearing a bulletproof vest at public events, citing fears of an attack similar to the one that struck his father, Jair Bolsonaro, in 2018. He justified the measure with the phrase: 'I can't give soup to luck,' meaning he refuses to leave his safety to chance.

item.title: Por que o impacto eleitoral da economia está diminuindo?
item.description: The electoral impact of the economy is declining due to partisan polarization, where voters' economic perceptions are strongly shaped by ideological loyalty rather than objective indicators. In 2022, two-thirds of Lula voters believed the economy had worsened, while only 10% of Bolsonaro voters agreed, demonstrating that economic evaluations are endogenous to partisan preference. This 'cheering' effect may intensify in 2026, making the economy less decisive in voting behavior than in past elections.

item.title: DPU pede anulação da ação contra Eduardo por parcialidade de Moraes
item.description: The Public Defender's Office (DPU) has requested the annulment of the case against Eduardo Bolsonaro, citing objective lack of impartiality by relator Alexandre de Moraes, who was personally affected by the investigations — including the revocation of his visa under the Magnitsky Act. The DPU, acting as Eduardo’s defense due to his lack of appointed counsel, argues his statements in the U.S. are protected by parliamentary immunity. The case stems from allegations of pressure on the Supreme Court related to the 2025 attempted coup investigation.

item.title: Quem era presidente municipal do PL que morreu após partida de futebol
item.description: Ademar Pahl Filho, known as Ademar Popeye, the municipal president of the Liberal Party (PL) in Navegantes (SC), died at age 40 after suffering a heart attack during a football match with friends. He was a businessman, digital influencer with over 27 thousand followers, a critic of President Lula’s government, and a supporter of Bolsonaro. His death was mourned by right-wing allies, including federal deputy Julia Zanatta and the PL of Santa Catarina.

item.title: Alerj rebate falas de Lula sobre “milícia organizada”
item.description: The Legislative Assembly of Rio de Janeiro (Alerj) responded to remarks by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who described the state legislature as an 'organized militia' during a Fiocruz event. In an official statement, Alerj said it respects institutions and expects the same respect from all national authorities, including the President of Brazil.

item.title: “Não posso dar sopa ao azar”, diz Flávio sobre colete à prova de balas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, pre-candidate for president and senator, said he wears a bulletproof vest because he 'can't give soup at random', referring to threats against himself and his family. He referenced the 2018 stabbing of his father, Jair Bolsonaro, and declared he is prepared to face those trying to intimidate him, without clearly identifying who 'they' are.

item.title: Fazenda Nacional cobra dívida de candidato a presidente da República
item.description: The National Treasury's Prosecutor's Office (PGFN) is pursuing a R$ 41,1 thousand tax debt linked to Martin Artefatos de Metais, a company where Renan Santos was a partner, registered in the Union's Active Debt for alleged irregular dissolution of a legal entity. The candidate denies liability, stating he joined the company in 2010 and left in October 2020, and that the debts originated in 2002/2003 under previous management. The PGFN has requested asset seizure via the Sisbajud system to recover the amount.

item.title: Flávio acena a Aldo depois de DC ameaçar tirá-lo da disputa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro reached out to Aldo Rebelo by phone as a gesture of sympathy amid Aldo’s internal struggles within the DC after party leader João Caldas nominated Joaquim Barbosa as a presidential pre-candidate. While no vice-presidential arrangement was discussed, allies are speculating about a potential alliance. Flávio also faces backlash from a leaked audio in which he asked for money from Daniel Vorcaro, who is imprisoned, prompting allies to urge him to strengthen his campaign with policy proposals and a running mate.

item.title: A resposta dos deputados que Lula chamou de ‘milicianos’ no Rio
item.description: President Lula called Rio state deputies 'militiamen' and demanded the arrest of governors linked to organized crime, prompting the Rio Legislative Assembly (Alerj) to reject his remarks as unacceptable and demand institutional respect. Alerj President Douglas Ruas (PL) accused Lula and Eduardo Paes of lacking moral authority on security, referencing Lula’s past comments about drug traffickers. The Alerj faces an image crisis after three deputies were arrested in under a year on suspicion of ties to militias.

item.title: Censura seria um prêmio para ‘Dark Horse’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) extended Lula's positive agenda at public expense by becoming entangled in explanations about his relationship with banker Daniel Vorcaro, a major sponsor of the film 'Dark Horse'. The collaboration between Lulists and Bolsonarists in the 2026 electoral race is described as mutually beneficial, with each side leveraging the other to boost their narratives. Censoring 'Dark Horse' would be seen as an indirect award, increasing the film's visibility and political impact.

item.title: Perfil do DC usou vídeo com IA de Joaquim Barbosa sem autorização
item.description: An Instagram profile linked to the Democracia Cristã party published an AI-generated video featuring former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa as a presidential pre-candidate without his authorization. The video also includes manipulated images of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and President Lula, sparking internal party conflict, as Aldo Rebelo, another pre-candidate, denounced the material as an 'affront' and threatened legal action if his candidacy is blocked.
